definitions.explanation: crescent-shaped dumplings with a thin wrapper filled with ground meat and vegetables, typically pan-fried

examples.japanese: {手作|てづく}りの{餃子|ぎょうざ}は{格別|かくべつ}においしい。
ラーメン{屋|や}で{餃子|ぎょうざ}をサイドメニューに{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I ordered gyoza as a side dish at the ramen shop.

notes:
JAPANESE FOOD CULTURE:
{餃子|ぎょうざ} is a popular Chinese-origin dish that has been adapted to Japanese tastes.

TYPES OF GYOZA:
- {焼|や}き{餃子|ぎょうざ} - pan-fried gyoza (most common in Japan)
- {水|すい}{餃子|ぎょうざ} - boiled dumplings
- {揚|あ}げ{餃子|ぎょうざ} - deep-fried gyoza
- {蒸|む}し{餃子|ぎょうざ} - steamed gyoza

FAMOUS GYOZA CITIES:
- {宇都宮|うつのみや} - Utsunomiya (famous gyoza city)
- {浜松|はままつ} - Hamamatsu

DIPPING SAUCE ({餃子|ぎょうざ}のタレ):
{酢|す} + {醤油|しょうゆ} + ラー{油|ゆ} (vinegar + soy sauce + chili oil)

COOKING TIPS:
- {羽根|はね}つき{餃子|ぎょうざ} - gyoza with crispy wings (made by adding starch water when frying)
